key_insight: Medical AI works best as a team: generalist LLMs, specialist models, and clinicians can outperform any single model alone.
clinical_relevance: For clinical decision support, combining broad reasoning with modality-specific specialists may improve accuracy, uncertainty handling, and when to escalate to human review.
method: Built HetMedAgent, a heterogeneous multi-agent framework for medical AI collaboration
Added conflict-aware evidence fusion to reconcile disagreements between models
Used uncertainty-based triggers and adaptive thresholds to decide when clinician intervention is needed
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on three real-world clinical decision-making tasks, where the combined generalist-plus-specialist approach outperformed either model type alone.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on reliable uncertainty estimation and careful threshold calibration, which may be hard to generalize across clinical settings.
paper_title: Why Specialist Models Still Matter: A Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Paradigm for Medical Artificial Intelligence
